80.t:
Client (المولى) of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
His mother: Ḥamāmah.
He was the muezzin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
One of the foremost early ones who were tormented for the sake of Allah; he was present at Badr, and the Prophet ﷺ testified for him by name that he would enter Paradise, and his hadith is in the Books.
Narrating from him: ابن عمر، وأبو عثمان النهدي، والأسود، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وجماعة.
His virtues are many; the hadith master (الحافظ) Ibn ʿAsākir covered them exhaustively.
He lived some sixty-odd years.
It is said: He was an Abyssinian.
It was also said: He was one of those born in the Hijaz.
There are several views on his death, one of them: in Dārayyā, in the year 20.
عاصم: عن زر، عن عبد الله:
The first who made their Islam public were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿAmmār, his mother Sumayyah, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and al-Miqdād.
As for the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr: Allah protected them through their people.
As for the rest of them, the polytheists seized them, ⟦1:347⟧ clothed them in coats of iron mail and scorched them in the sun. There was not one of them who did not give them what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his own self became of little worth to him for the sake of Allah, and he was of little worth to his people. So they handed him over to the boys, who took him around the ravines of Mecca while he kept saying: One, One (1) .
He has another authentic (الصحيح) chain of transmission (الإسناد).
أبو حيان التيمي: عن أبي زرعة، عن أبي هريرة:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Bilāl at the time of the dawn prayer: (Tell me of the most hopeful deed you have done in Islam, for last night I heard the sound of your sandals ahead of me in Paradise) .
He said: I have done no deed more hopeful than this: I have never purified myself completely at any hour of night or day without praying for my Lord whatever was decreed for me to pray (2) .
حسين بن واقد: حدثنا ابن بريدة، سمعت أبي يقول:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the morning and called Bilāl, and said: (By what did you precede me to Paradise? I have never entered Paradise without hearing the rustle of your steps ahead of me. I entered Paradise last night and heard the rustle of your steps ahead of me, and I came upon a palace of gold, and I said: Whose is this?
They said: ʿUmar's) .
Bilāl said: I have never given the call to prayer without praying two rakʿahs, and no ritual impurity has befallen me without my performing ablution, and I considered that I owed Allah two rakʿahs that I should pray.
He said: (By them) (3) . ⟦1:348⟧
Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Thābit:
from Anas, raised (المرفوع): (I entered Paradise and heard footsteps.
I said: What is this?
It was said: Bilāl (1)) .
عمارة بن زاذان: عن ثابت، عن أنس:
that the Prophet ﷺ said: (The forerunners are four: I am the forerunner of the Arabs, Salmān is the forerunner of the Persians, Bilāl is the forerunner of the Abyssinians, and Ṣuhayb is the forerunner of the Byzantines (2)) .
Al-Masʿūdī, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said:
The first to give the call to prayer was Bilāl (3) .
ابن المنكدر: عن جابر، قال عمر:
Abū Bakr is our master, and he freed our master, Bilāl (4) .
ʿUmar ibn Ḥamzah, from Sālim:
that a poet praised Bilāl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, saying:
And Bilāl of ʿAbd Allāh is the best of Bilāls ...
Ibn ʿUmar said: You are wrong; rather: And Bilāl of the Messenger of Allah is the best of Bilāls. ⟦1:349⟧
In the hadith of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah (1) : I said: Who has followed you?
He said: (A free man and a slave) .
And there with him were: Abū Bakr and Bilāl (2) .
On the patronymic (الكنية) of Bilāl there are three views: Abū ʿAbd al-Karīm, Abū ʿAbd Allāh and Abū ʿAmr.
The hadith master (الحافظ) Abū al-Qāsim transmitted them. ⟦1:350⟧
He said: Narrating from him: أبو بكر، وعمر، وأسامة بن زيد، وابن عمر، وكعب بن عجرة، والصنابحي، والأسود، وأبو إدريس الخولاني، وسعيد بن المسيب، وابن أبي ليلى، والحكم بن مينا، وأبو عثمان النهدي.
Ayyūb ibn Sayyār, one of the worthless, said: عن محمد بن المنكدر، عن جابر، عن أبي بكر، عن بلال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Pray the dawn prayer when the dawn is bright, for it brings greater reward (1)) .
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: Bilāl ibn ʿAbd Allāh was one of those born in al-Sarāh; his mother Ḥamāmah belonged to the Banū Jumaḥ (2) .
Al-Bukhārī said: Bilāl, the brother of Khālid and Ghufrah (3) , the muezzin of the Prophet ﷺ, died in Syria. And he mentioned the three patronymics (الكنية). ⟦1:351⟧
ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: I was with Ibn al-Musayyib, and he mentioned Bilāl and said:
He was tenacious of his religion, and he was being tormented for the sake of Allah. He met the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (If we had anything, we would buy Bilāl) .
Then Abū Bakr met al-ʿAbbās and said: Buy Bilāl for me.
So al-ʿAbbās bought him and sent him to Abū Bakr, who freed him (1) .
محمد بن خالد الطحان: أنبأنا أبي، عن داود، عن الشعبي، قال:
Bilāl's masters used to lay him down on his stomach, squeeze him and say: Your religion is al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
He would say: My Lord is Allah, One, One; and if I knew a word more infuriating to you than it, I would say it.
Abū Bakr passed by them, and they said: Buy your brother in your religion.
So he bought him for forty ounces and freed him.
They said: Had he refused to pay more than one ounce, we would have sold him.
He said: I swear by Allah, had you refused to take less than such-and-such - a great amount - I would have bought him (2) .
In the Sīrah: Abū Bakr bought him from Umayyah ibn Khalaf in exchange for a black polytheist slave (3) .
Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said:
Waraqah ibn Nawfal passed by Bilāl while he was being tormented for Islam, his back pressed against the scorching sand, and he was saying: One, One.
He said: O Bilāl! Patience! By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you kill him, I shall take him as an object of tender devotion (4) .
This is mursal (مرسل), and Waraqah did not live until that time.
Hishām, from Ibn Sīrīn:
that when Bilāl's masters learned of his Islam, they stretched him out in ⟦1:352⟧ the sun and tormented him, and they kept saying: Your god is al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
And he kept saying: One, One.
This reached Abū Bakr, so he came to them and said: Why are you killing him? He will not obey you.
They said: Buy him.
So he bought him for seven ounces and freed him (1) .
He told the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (A partnership, O Abū Bakr!) .
He said: I have already freed him (2) .
ابن عيينة: عن إسماعيل، عن قيس، قال:
Abū Bakr bought Bilāl, while he was buried under stones, for five ounces of gold.
They said: Had you refused to pay more than one ounce, we would have sold him to you.
He said: Had you refused to take less than a hundred ounces, I would have taken him (3) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is strong.
إسرائيل (4) : عن المقدام بن شريح، عن أبيه، عن سعد، قال:
We were six men with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The polytheists said: Drive these away from you, so that they do not presume against us.
They were I, Ibn Masʿūd, Bilāl, a man from Hudhayl, and two others.
So Allah revealed: “And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord ...”, the two verses [al-Anʿām: 52, 53] (5) . ⟦1:353⟧
ابن علية: عن يونس، عن الحسن:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Bilāl is the forerunner of the Abyssinians (1)) .
ʿĀʾishah said: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, Abū Bakr and Bilāl fell ill, and whenever the fever took hold of Abū Bakr he would say:
Every man is greeted in the morning among his family ... while death is nearer to him than the strap of his sandal
And whenever it left Bilāl, he would raise his voice and say:
Would that I knew whether I shall spend a night ... in a valley with idhkhir and jalīl around me,
and whether I shall one day come down to the waters of Majannah ... and whether Shāmah and Ṭafīl will appear to me.
O Allah, curse ʿUtbah, Shaybah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, as they drove us out of our land to the land of pestilence (2) .
الحسن بن صالح: عن أبي ربيعة، عن الحسن، عن أنس، قال: The Messenger of ⟦1:354⟧ Allah ﷺ said: (Paradise longs for three: ʿAlī, ʿAmmār and Bilāl (1)) .
Abū Rabīʿah ʿUmar ibn Rabīʿah al-Iyādī: weak (ضعيف).
حسام بن مصك (2) : عن قتادة، عن القاسم بن ربيعة:
from Zayd ibn Arqam, who traced it back to the Prophet: (What an excellent man Bilāl is, the master of the muezzins on the Day of Resurrection; and the muezzins will have the longest necks of all people on the Day of Resurrection (3)) .
It has other weak (ضعيف) routes.
It is narrated with a flimsy chain of transmission (الإسناد), among the mursal (مرسل) reports of Kathīr ibn Murrah: (Bilāl will be brought (4) a she-camel from the she-camels of Paradise, and he will ride it) .
Ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd (5) ibn Jābir:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The masters of the black people are: Luqmān, the Negus, Bilāl and Mihjaʿ) (6) . ⟦1:355⟧
Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated it from al-Awzāʿī as muʿḍal (المعضل) (1) .
Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered Bilāl at the time of the Conquest, and he gave the call to prayer on top of the Kaʿbah (2) .
Ibn Saʿd said: حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبي أويس، حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن عمار المؤذن، حدثني ابن عمي عبد الله (3) بن محمد، وعمار بن حفص، وأخوه عمر، عن آبائهم، عن أجدادهم:
that the Negus sent three short spears to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He gave one to ʿAlī and one to ʿUmar, and kept one. Bilāl used to walk with it in front of him on the two ʿĪds until he reached the prayer ground, where he would plant it in front of him and he would pray facing it. Then he used to walk with it in front of Abū Bakr, and then Saʿd al-Qaraẓ used to walk with it in front of ʿUmar and ʿUthmān.
They said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, Bilāl came, wanting to go on jihad (4) , to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and said to him:
O Successor of the Messenger of Allah! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: (The best deed of the believer is jihad in the path of Allah) .
Abū Bakr said: So what do you wish, O Bilāl?
He said: I want to stand guard on the frontier in the path of Allah until I die.
Abū Bakr said: I adjure you by Allah, O Bilāl, and by my sanctity and my right: I have grown old and weak, and my appointed time has drawn near.
So he stayed with him until he died.
Then he came to ʿUmar, who answered him as Abū Bakr had, but Bilāl refused. ⟦1:356⟧ ʿUmar said: To whom do you think I should assign the call to prayer?
He said: To Saʿd, for he gave the call to prayer for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
So ʿUmar assigned it to Saʿd and his descendants (1) .
حماد بن سلمة: عن علي بن زيد، عن سعيد بن المسيب:
that when Abū Bakr sat on the pulpit on Friday, Bilāl said to him:
Did you free me for Allah or for yourself?
He said: For Allah.
He said: Then give me leave to go on military campaigns.
So he gave him leave, and he went to Syria and died there (2) .
محمد بن نصر المروزي: حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الرحمن القرشي، حدثنا الوليد بن مسلم، أخبرني سعيد بن عبد العزيز، وابن جابر، وغيرهما:
that Bilāl did not give the call to prayer for anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He wanted to go on jihad, and Abū Bakr wanted to prevent him.
He said: If you freed me for Allah, then let me go my way.
He said: He was in Syria until ʿUmar came to al-Jābiyah, and the Muslims asked ʿUmar to ask Bilāl on their behalf to give the call to prayer for them.
So he asked him, and he gave the call to prayer one day, and no day was ever seen with more people weeping than that day, out of their remembrance of the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Walīd said: We hold that the call to prayer of the people of Syria derives from his call to prayer that day (3) .
هشام بن سعد: عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، قال:
We came to Syria with ʿUmar, and Bilāl gave the call to prayer, and the people remembered the Prophet ﷺ, and I have never seen a day with more people weeping than it.
أبو أحمد الحاكم (4) : أنبأنا محمد بن الفيض بدمشق، حدثنا أبو إسحاق ⟦1:357⟧ إبراهيم بن محمد بن سليمان بن أبي الدرداء، حدثني أبي، عن جدي سليمان، عن أم الدرداء، عن أبي الدرداء، قال:
When ʿUmar entered Syria, Bilāl asked him to let him settle there, and he did so.
He said: And my brother Abū Ruwayḥah, between whom and me the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood. He settled in Dārayyā among Khawlān, and he and his brother went to a group of Khawlān and said:
We have come to you as suitors. We were unbelievers and Allah guided us, slaves and Allah freed us, poor and Allah enriched us. If you marry us, then praise be to Allah; and if you turn us away, then there is no might and no power except with Allah.
So they married them.
Then Bilāl saw the Prophet ﷺ in his sleep, saying: (What is this estrangement, O Bilāl? Has the time not come for you to visit me?) .
He woke up sad, mounted his riding camel and headed for Medina. He came to the grave of the Prophet ﷺ and began weeping at it and rubbing his face on it. Then al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn came, and he began hugging them and kissing them.
They said to him: O Bilāl! We long to hear your call to prayer.
So he did so: he climbed onto the roof and stood.
When he said: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Medina shook.
When he said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, its shaking increased.
When he said: I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, the young maidens came out of their private quarters.
And they said: The Messenger of Allah has been raised back to life!
No day was ever seen in Medina with more men and women weeping after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than that day (1) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is soft in hadith (لين الحديث), and it is rejected (المنكر).
قتيبة: حدثنا الليث، عن يحيى بن سعيد (2) ، قال:
ʿUmar mentioned the merit of Abū Bakr, ⟦1:358⟧ and began (1) to describe his virtues.
Then he said: And this Bilāl, our master, is one of his good deeds.
أبو هشام الرفاعي: حدثنا ابن فضيل، حدثنا إسماعيل، عن قيس، قال:
It reached Bilāl that some people were ranking him above Abū Bakr, and he said: How can they rank me above him, when I am only one of his good deeds?!
الواقدي: حدثنا سعيد بن عبد العزيز، عن مكحول، قال:
Someone who saw Bilāl told me: he was a dark-brown man, intensely dark, slender, tall, slightly stooped (2) , with abundant hair and thin on the cheeks, with much grey in it, and he did not dye it (3) .
It was also said: Bilāl was the same age as Abū Bakr.
Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: When death came upon Bilāl, he said:
Tomorrow we shall meet the loved ones ... Muḥammad and his party
He said: His wife was saying: O woe!
And he said: O joy!
Muḥammad ibn (4) Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, Ibn Isḥāq, Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr and a group said:
Bilāl died in the year 20 in Damascus.
Al-Wāqidī said: He was buried at Bāb al-Ṣaghīr, and he was some sixty-odd years old.
ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tamīmī said: He was buried at Bāb Kaysān (5) .
Ibn Zayd said: He was carried from Dārayyā and buried at Bāb Kaysān.
It was also said: He died in the year ⟦1:359⟧ 21.
Marwān ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāṭarī said: Bilāl died in Dārayyā, was carried, and was buried at Bāb al-Ṣaghīr.
ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Muḥammad said in (Tārīkh Dārayyā) : I heard a group from Khawlān saying:
His grave is in Dārayyā, in the cemetery of Khawlān.
As for ʿUthmān ibn Khurrazādh (1) , he said:
حدثنا محمد بن أبي أسامة الحلبي، حدثنا أبو سعد الأنصاري، عن علي بن عبد الرحمن، قال:
Bilāl died in Aleppo and was buried at Bāb al-Arbaʿīn.
Forty-four hadiths have come from him; of them, in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين)) : four; agreed upon (المتفق عليه): one.
Al-Bukhārī alone has two hadiths, and Muslim alone one halted (الموقوف) hadith.
